sections.title: Core Foundations & Conceptual Framework
sections.content:
• **All-India Federation Principle**: Proposed a federation comprising British Indian Provinces and **Princely States**, though it never materialized due to optional joining clauses for princes.
• **Abolition of Dyarchy at Provinces**: **Provincial Autonomy** was introduced, ending dyarchy at the provincial level and granting independent administrative spheres to provincial cabinets.
• **Introduction of Dyarchy at Center**: Transferred and Reserved subjects were demarcated at the federal level, though the federal portion of the Act was never implemented.
• **Key Metric / Factor**: Out of 321 sections and 10 schedules, nearly 250 provisions were directly adopted or adapted into the 1950 Constitution of India.

items.definition: Abolition of dyarchy in provinces; provinces were recognized as autonomous units of administration in their defined spheres, accountable to provincial legislatures.
Established in Delhi in 1937 with original, appellate, and advisory jurisdiction, serving as the precursor to the Federal Court/Supreme Court of independent India.
Statutory body established under the Act in 1935 to control India's currency, credit, and monetary policy.
Expanded separate electorates beyond Muslims to include Depressed Classes (Scheduled Castes), Women, and Labour, fracturing nationalist unity.

items.title: Major Geographical Distribution / Regional Hubs
items.content:
• **New Provinces Created**: Sindh separated from Bombay, and Orissa separated from Bihar.
• **Burma Separation**: Burma (Myanmar) was formally separated from British India under this Act.
• **North-West Frontier Province (NWFP)**: Elevated to the status of a full Governor's province with a legislative assembly.

items.title: Challenges, Reforms & Forward Strategy
items.content:
• **Bottlenecks / Issues**: Excessive discretionary powers and overriding vetoes vested in the Governor-General and Provincial Governors.
• **Policy Interventions**: Comprehensive franchise expansion (about 10% of the population voting) and creation of Public Service Commissions (Federal, Provincial, and Joint).

items.title: Mnemonic for Federal Lists (FPF)
items.content:
• **Memory Acronym / Phrase**: **F**ederal, **P**rovincial, **F**ederal-Concurrent.
• **Decoded Meaning**: Federal List = Center, Provincial List = Province, Concurrent List = Both.
• **Prelims Exam Value**: Instantly eliminates confusion regarding residual powers, which were vested solely in the Viceroy/Governor-General.

items.title: Retention Rule of Thumb
items.content: • **Core Formula / Rule**: Remember **'No Federation, Yes Autonomy'**—the All-India Federation part failed because princely states refused to join, but provincial autonomy was successfully implemented in 1937.

upscNotes.content: Examiner Trap: UPSC frequently states that the All-India Federation envisaged under the 1935 Act came into operation. Remember that the federal part **never** came into effect due to non-fulfillment of conditions by princely states.

Mains Value Addition: Analyze the 1935 Act as a paradox—while it introduced responsible government and democratic space at the provincial level, it retained autocratic imperial safeguards through gubernatorial vetoes and ordinances.

keyTakeaways: The Government of India Act 1935 laid the structural and administrative foundation of independent India's Constitution.
It abolished dyarchy in the provinces, introduced provincial autonomy, and proposed an unfulfilled All-India Federation.
It introduced bicameralism in major provinces, expanded communal electorates, and established the Federal Court and RBI.
